prerequisites: Knowledge of the fundamentals of electrical engineering (lectures Electronics 1 and 2): Two-pole theory, network analysis (DC and AC), components (resistor, diode, transistor, capacitance and inductance), basic circuits with operational amplifiers, frequency response, Boolean algebra

learning_outcomes.text: Students can translate logical expressions into electronic circuits, analyze and build simple logic circuits, understand common circuit solutions and adapt these circuits to changed boundary conditions.
Students have gained in-depth knowledge in digital electronics (e.g. ADC and DAC) using practical examples.

Participants can apply fundamental theoretical and practical methods of power electronics for electrical machines by knowing how batteries are charged from the electrical grid using power electronics to efficiently utilize the energy used.

syllabus_topics: Review of transistors: Differential amplifiers, amplification of differential signals with common-mode rejection
Digital Electronics: Analog vs. digital, from transistor to IC, elementary switching algebra, arithmetic operations, representation of information by bit patterns
Logic Families: TTL family, CMOS family, comparison of logic families

Memory Circuits (Flip-Flops): RS flip-flop, Master/Slave-RS flip-flop, D flip-flop, transparent JK master/slave flip-flop, edge-triggered JK flip-flop, universality of JK flip-flops, LED for indicating voltage levels
Counters: Asynchronous counters, asynchronous MOD-n counters, asynchronous counter ICs, synchronous counters
Shift Registers: Ring registers, shift register ICs, shift register application
Multivibrators and the 555-timer: Capacitor charging and discharging, comparator circuit, Timer 555, astable multivibrator, switching times, monostable multivibrator, bistable multivibrator

Digital Converters: General properties, sample-and-hold circuit, important characteristic values and conversion errors, basic principles of A/D conversion, parallel method, counting method, weighing method, dual-slope method, comparison of converter methods, Digital/Analog converters, D/A converter IC, audio-visual examples, sampling theorem, sampling, reconstruction and sampling theorem, aliasing
Advanced Operational Amplifier Circuits: Integrator, precision rectifier, current source with OPV and transistors, offset adjustment, swing of OPV, blocking of interference, reflections
Transistor Circuits: Dimensioning of an LED, current amplification in transistors, push/pull circuit (complementary symmetry circuit)
Fundamentals of Digital Electronics: NAND gate, NOR gate, RS flip-flop, D flip-flop, asynchronous counter, shift register
Multivibrator Circuits: RC filter circuit, series resonant circuit, timer (astable multivibrator, monostable multivibrator)
Analog/Digital Converters: 4-bit D/A converter, 4-bit A/D converter using the weighing method, 4-bit A/D converter using the parallel method, A/D converter IC with bar display
assessment_rules: The module examination is a graded written exam of 90 minutes duration. Laboratory reports for MECB332 are ungraded. The module grade for MECB330 corresponds to the grade of MECB331 (the lecture).
